title: Most Americans think artificial intelligence is developing too fast, a new AP-NORC poll finds
source_used: KEYE / CBS Austin (The National News Desk) report on the AP-NORC poll
key_facts: An AP-NORC poll found 64% of Americans think AI is developing too fast, 27% say about right, 8% say too slow.
Nearly 80% said it is at least very important for the government to keep AI under human control and to protect the workforce.
About 40% trust neither party to handle AI; nearly 2 in 10 trust both equally.
A Reuters-Ipsos poll released Wednesday found a majority think the Trump administration and Congress are not concerned enough about AI.
Congress left for the midterm campaign with no significant AI legislation passed.
quote_evidence: A new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs research found 64% of Americans think it is developing too fast, while only 27% think it has been “about right” and 8% said it was too slow.

Around 40% of Americans said they don’t trust either party to handle AI, while nearly 2 in 10 said they trusted both parties equally and the rest split between which side was better, according to the AP-NORC poll.
why_it_matters_hint: Public opinion is running well ahead of Washington on AI rules, just before the midterms.
